          Liga F, Frauen-Bundesliga, Première Ligue, Serie A Opta Supercomputer Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 16, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We explore the Opta supercomputer’s predictions for Europe’s women’s leagues: the Frauen-Bundesliga, Liga F, Première Ligue and Serie A.

As the first international break of the second half of the year comes to a close, domestic football across Europe resumes this weekend, and the Opta supercomputer has simulated the season ahead across the continent’s leading women’s leagues.

Having already explored our WSL season predictions, we now turn our attention to the rest of Europe’s top five leagues: Spain’s Liga F, Germany’s Frauen-Bundesliga, Italy’s Serie A and France’s Première Ligue.
Six matches have been played in Spain and Germany, France has completed four rounds of fixtures, and Italy’s campaign is only just getting under way after kicking off at the end of September.

Barcelona are overwhelming favourites to retain their Liga F crown, while OL Lyonnes and Bayern Munich look firmly in control in France and Germany. Italy, meanwhile, appears to offer us the closest title race of the four.
Using 10,000 simulations for each league, we break down the Opta supercomputer’s predictions to assess who is best placed to claim silverware, secure European qualification and avoid relegation.

The Frauen-Bundesliga may not command the same global attention as the NWSL or WSL, but Opta’s Power Rankings place it as the third-best league in the world. With the German season kicking off on 21 August, we're already six games into the new campaign.

The Opta supercomputer forecasts a two-horse race between Bayern Munich and VfL Wolfsburg, although whether the contest will prove competitive remains to be seen. Bayern finished 16 points clear last season, the largest winning margin in league history, and are overwhelming favourites to retain their crown.

The Bavarians are projected to win the title in 92.9% of the supercomputer’s 10,000 simulations. They are the only side to have maintained a 100% record after six matches. Bayern are bidding to become the first team in the division’s history to win five consecutive league titles.

Wolfsburg remain their closest challengers, though they only have a 6.4% probability of lifting the trophy. They have collected 15 points from a possible 18 so far, though, after losing to TSG Hoffenheim 2-1 on Matchday 5, their first loss against the side since March 2024.
It means that Stephan Lerch’s side are projected to finish second in 67.5% of simulations and have a 93.3% chance of qualifying for the UEFA Women’s Champions League (UWCL).

Wolfsburg’s attacking quality has been evident, with Ella Peddemors leading the league for attacking-sequence involvements (42) and goals scored (four), while teammate Svenja Huth has created more chances than any other player (29). They also top the league for high turnovers (76) and shots following high turnovers (17), underlining their ability to win possession high up the pitch and turn pressure into clear-cut opportunities.
The battle for Europe sees four clubs competing for the three available UWCL places.

Bayern are guaranteed to qualify according to the model, while Wolfsburg (93.3%), Eintracht Frankfurt (62.8%) and Bayer Leverkusen (35.6%) are the other leading contenders. However, qualification does not guarantee a direct route into the competition: only the Bundesliga champions secure direct entry to the UWCL league phase, with the other places entering through earlier qualifying rounds.
Leverkusen look increasingly dangerous this season, particularly away from home, having won six consecutive matches on the road; their longest such streak in league history.

Erëleta Memeti has been instrumental in their progress, leading the league for goal involvements (seven), expected assists (3.68), big chances created (four) and successful dribbles (16), highlighting her influence as both a creator and a ball-carrier.

The 2025-26 campaign also marked a significant change for the division, which expanded from 12 to 14 teams, mirroring the WSL’s recent expansion. This season has brought two historic arrivals, with VfB Stuttgart and 1. FSV Mainz 05 competing in the top flight for the first time.
Stuttgart have made an encouraging start to life among the elite, sitting eighth with eight points after six matches.

Their games included a narrow 2-1 defeat to Wolfsburg, demonstrating their ability to compete against established Bundesliga sides. Their points tally is the most by a promoted team at this stage since Bayern Munich collected 12 points after six games in 2000-01.

That promising start is reflected in Opta’s projections. Stuttgart have just a 2.9% probability of finishing bottom and a 13% chance of relegation, placing them among the more secure sides in the lower half of the table.
